title: How do we write repeated letters and a big number as powers?
description: Repeated letters are written in short with exponents, and then thirty two thousand four hundred is split into primes, written with exponents. Keeko's doubt is that eigh times eigh is two eigh.
teaching_notes: One idea: repeated multiplication of the same letter or the same prime is counted and written as a power. Watch for students who write eigh times eigh as two eigh.

source: Write a × a × b × b × b × b in exponential form, and express
video_script.why: The child can write a repeated multiplication of one number as a power and now writes letters and a prime split of a big number the same way.
video_script.substitution: The book's own letters a and b, and the book's own number thirty two thousand four hundred.
video_script.anchor: the repeated letters on the board, and the number thirty two thousand four hundred being divided by primes one after another
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks eigh times eigh is two eigh, which is eigh added to itself. A power counts how many times the letter is multiplied.
video_script.payoff_line: The number is two to the power four, times five squared, times three to the power four

final_answer.spoken: eigh squared bee to the power four, and thirty two thousand four hundred is two to the power four, times five squared, times three to the power four

maths_rules: a × a × b × b × b × b = a²b⁴ (two a's, four b's)
video_script.design: One idea: count each repeated factor and write the count as the exponent. The letters and the number stay on the board all video; the prime split is done one prime at a time; one slip at the end.

beats.on_screen: title card, From your book; a × a × b × b × b × b on the board, and 32400 beside it

marks.book: the title card From your book arrives
marks.letters: a × a × b × b × b × b appears on the board
marks.ask: 32400 appears beside it with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about repeated multiplication.
<bookmark mark='letters'/>The board shows eigh times eigh times bee times bee times bee times bee.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write that in short?
And how can we write thirty two thousand four hundred in the same short way?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 in a row, each with only two factors, 1 and itself; the label prime number

marks.two: the factors 1 and the number itself are shown for 7
marks.prime: the label prime number is written under the row

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Some numbers have only two factors, one and the number itself.
<bookmark mark='prime'/>Such a number is called a prime number.
Two, three, five and seven are prime numbers.

beats.on_screen: Given: a × a × b × b × b × b; 32400

marks.given: the letters and the number are written in the working area

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the letters eigh and bee multiplied as shown, and thirty two thousand four hundred.

beats.on_screen: To find: the letters in short form; 32400 as powers of primes
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the letters in short form.
We also write the number using powers of primes.

beats.on_screen: a × a → a²; b × b × b × b → b⁴; so a × a × b × b × b × b = a²b⁴

marks.one: the repeated a's and b's are counted: two a's, four b's

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, eigh is multiplied twice, and bee is multiplied four times.
<bookmark mark='short'/>In short, that is eigh squared bee to the power four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, divide thirty two thousand four hundred by two.
Sixteen thousand two hundred, then eight thousand one hundred.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Then four thousand fifty, then two thousand twenty five.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>Two divided out four times, and two thousand twenty five is odd.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, divide two thousand twenty five by five.
<bookmark mark='twice'/>That gives four hundred five, then eighty one.
Five divided out twice, and eighty one does not divide by five.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, divide eighty one by three, again and again.
<bookmark mark='end'/>That gives twenty seven, nine, three and one.
Three divided out four times.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>In short, it is eigh squared bee to the power four.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The number is two to the power four, times five squared, times three to the power four.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check: sixteen times twenty five times eighty one is thirty two thousand four hundred.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the letters
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a × a = 2a appears, then is crossed out; a × a = a² is written, and a + a = 2a is written beside it

marks.fix: 2a is crossed out, a × a = a² is written, and a + a = 2a is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks eigh times eigh is two eigh.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But two eigh is eigh added to itself.
Eigh times eigh is eigh squared, because eigh is multiplied by itself.
